syllabus.subject: G3 English Language

assessment.format: Editing for grammatical errors, situational writing (250–350 words, based on a visual text) and continuous writing (350–500 words, one of four topics).
Comprehension, vocabulary in context and language for effect across Texts 1–4, including an 80-word summary.
Varied listening tasks and a simple note-taking exercise on a recording heard once.
A planned response of up to 2 minutes to a video clip and prompt, then a discussion with the examiners.

topics.title: Writing: Editing
outcomes: Identify grammatical errors in a short continuous text
Write corrections (punctuation and spelling are not tested here)

topics.title: Writing: Situational Writing
outcomes: Write 250–350 words for a given situation with a visual text
Suit purpose, audience and context (email, letter, report, speech)
Use the given information to support ideas

topics.title: Writing: Continuous Writing
outcomes: Write 350–500 words on one of four topics
Address all parts of the task in detail
Organise ideas coherently with accurate language

topics.title: Reading: Comprehension
outcomes: Understand texts at literal, inferential and evaluative levels
Explain the use of language for effect

topics.title: Summary Writing
outcomes: Write an 80-word summary in your own words

topics.title: Listening
outcomes: Understand audio texts at literal, inferential and evaluative levels
Take simple notes from an informational recording

topics.title: Speaking: Planned Response
outcomes: Plan a response to a video clip and prompt
Deliver a fluent response of up to 2 minutes
Use clear pronunciation and appropriate intonation

topics.title: Speaking: Spoken Interaction
outcomes: Discuss a topic related to the video with examiners
Develop perspectives in response to prompts

topics.title: Grammar and Vocabulary
outcomes: Understand how language creates meaning and impact

topics.title: Text Types
outcomes: Read narrative, recount, non-narrative, visual and multimodal texts
Write for different purposes and audiences

syllabus.notes: Candidates sit all four papers (180 marks); Paper 4 is computer-based.

syllabus.subject: G3 Mathematics

assessment.format: About 26 short-answer questions, all compulsory.
9 to 10 questions of varying marks and lengths, all compulsory; the last question applies mathematics to a real-world scenario.

topics.title: Numbers and their operations
outcomes: Use primes, prime factorisation, HCF and LCM
Work with integers, rational and real numbers and their four operations
Use standard form and the laws of indices
Represent and order numbers on a number line

topics.title: Ratio and proportion
outcomes: Write and simplify ratios involving rational numbers
Use map scales for distance and area
Solve direct and inverse proportion problems

topics.title: Percentage
outcomes: Express one quantity as a percentage of another
Increase or decrease a quantity by a given percentage

topics.title: Rate and speed
outcomes: Calculate average rate and average speed
Convert units such as km/h to m/s

topics.title: Algebraic expressions and formulae
outcomes: Interpret algebraic notation and translate situations into expressions
Evaluate formulae and change the subject of a formula
Simplify, expand and factorise linear and quadratic expressions
Find an expression for the nth term of a pattern
Use the square and difference of two squares identities

topics.title: Functions and graphs
outcomes: Plot and interpret graphs of linear and quadratic functions
Find the gradient of a linear graph
Sketch quadratic graphs and find maximum or minimum points
Estimate the gradient of a curve by drawing a tangent

topics.title: Equations and inequalities
outcomes: Solve linear and simple fractional equations
Solve simultaneous linear equations algebraically and graphically
Solve quadratic equations by factorising, formula, completing the square or graphing
Solve fractional equations that reduce to quadratics
Solve linear inequalities and show solutions on a number line

topics.title: Set language and notation
outcomes: Use set notation for union, intersection, complement and subsets
Count elements of a set using n(A)

topics.title: Matrices
outcomes: Display information in the form of a matrix
Interpret data in a given matrix
Multiply a matrix by a scalar
Add and multiply matrices where appropriate

topics.title: Angles, triangles and polygons
outcomes: Recognise angle types and angle relationships on lines, at points and between parallel lines
Use properties of triangles, special quadrilaterals and regular polygons
Find interior and exterior angle sums of convex polygons
Construct simple figures using compasses, ruler, set squares and protractor

topics.title: Congruence and similarity
outcomes: Use properties of similar triangles and polygons
Find ratios of areas and volumes of similar figures
Enlarge, reduce and draw scale drawings
Construct perpendicular bisectors and angle bisectors
Determine whether two triangles are congruent or similar

topics.title: Properties of circles
outcomes: Use symmetry properties of chords and tangents
Use the angle in a semicircle and tangent-radius properties
Use angle properties of circles, including angles in the same or opposite segments

topics.title: Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry
outcomes: Use Pythagoras' theorem and test whether a triangle is right-angled
Use sine, cosine and tangent, including for obtuse angles
Find the area of a triangle using one-half ab sin C
Use the sine rule and cosine rule
Solve two- and three-dimensional problems involving elevation, depression and bearings

topics.title: Mensuration
outcomes: Find areas and perimeters of plane figures, including composite figures
Find volumes and surface areas of common solids
Convert between cm² and m², and between cm³ and m³
Calculate arc length, sector area and segment area
Use radian measure and convert between radians and degrees

topics.title: Coordinate geometry
outcomes: Find the gradient and length of a line segment from coordinates
Find the equation of a straight line in the form y = mx + c

topics.title: Vectors in two dimensions
outcomes: Use vector notation and represent vectors as directed line segments
Find the magnitude of a vector
Add, subtract and multiply vectors by a scalar

topics.title: Data handling and analysis
outcomes: Analyse and interpret tables, graphs and charts, including histograms, stem-and-leaf and box-and-whisker plots
Calculate mean, mode, median, quartiles and percentiles
Calculate range, interquartile range and standard deviation
Compare data sets and explain misleading diagrams

topics.title: Probability
outcomes: Understand probability as a measure of chance
Find probabilities by listing possible outcomes
Use possibility and tree diagrams for combined events
Add and multiply probabilities for mutually exclusive and independent events

syllabus.notes: An approved calculator may be used in both papers, candidates must bring geometrical instruments, and relevant formulae are provided in the question papers.

syllabus.subject: G3 Additional Mathematics

assessment.format: 12 to 14 questions of varying marks and lengths, up to 10 marks each, all compulsory.
9 to 11 questions of varying marks and lengths, up to 12 marks each, all compulsory.

topics.title: Quadratic functions
outcomes: Find the maximum or minimum value of a quadratic by completing the square
Determine when a quadratic expression is always positive or always negative

topics.title: Equations and inequalities
outcomes: Determine conditions for a quadratic equation to have two real roots, equal roots, or no real roots
Determine conditions for a line to intersect, be a tangent to, or not intersect a curve
Solve simultaneous equations in two variables by substitution, with one equation linear
Solve quadratic inequalities and show solutions on a number line

topics.title: Surds
outcomes: Perform the four operations on surds

topics.title: Polynomials and partial fractions
outcomes: Use the remainder and factor theorems to factorise polynomials and solve cubic equations
Use the sum and difference of cubes formulae
Resolve rational expressions into partial fractions with linear, repeated linear, and linear-times-quadratic denominators

topics.title: Binomial expansions
outcomes: Use the Binomial Theorem for positive integer n
Use factorial and binomial coefficient notation
Find a general term of a binomial expansion

topics.title: Exponential and logarithmic functions
outcomes: Understand the graphs and laws of exponential and logarithmic functions
Convert between exponential and logarithmic forms
Simplify expressions and solve simple exponential and logarithmic equations
Use exponential and logarithmic functions as models

topics.title: Trigonometric functions, identities and equations
outcomes: Use the six trigonometric functions for angles of any size in degrees or radians
Find principal values of inverse trigonometric functions and exact values for special angles
Understand amplitude, periodicity and symmetry, and sketch transformed sine, cosine and tangent graphs
Use standard identities and compound angle, double angle and R-form expressions
Solve simple trigonometric equations in a given interval and prove simple identities

topics.title: Coordinate geometry in two dimensions
outcomes: Determine conditions for lines to be parallel or perpendicular and find midpoints
Find the area of a rectilinear figure
Work with circles in standard and general forms
Transform relationships to linear form to find unknown constants from a straight line graph

topics.title: Proofs in plane geometry
outcomes: Use properties of parallel lines, perpendiculars, angle bisectors, triangles, special quadrilaterals and circles
Use properties of congruent and similar triangles

topics.title: Differentiation and integration
outcomes: Differentiate standard functions, products, quotients and composite functions
Use derivatives for gradients, tangents, normals, rates of change, and increasing or decreasing functions
Find and classify stationary points and solve maxima and minima problems
Integrate standard functions and evaluate definite integrals
Find areas under and below the x-axis and between curves and lines
Apply calculus to displacement, velocity and acceleration of a particle moving in a straight line

syllabus.notes: An approved calculator may be used in both papers, relevant formulae are provided, and omitting essential working results in lost marks.

syllabus.subject: G3 Physics

assessment.format: 40 compulsory multiple-choice items.
Section A (70 marks): compulsory structured questions, the last two worth 20 marks including a data-based question of 8–12 marks; Section B (10 marks): answer one of two questions.
Practical test in two 20-mark sections, some questions assessing planning and data analysis.

topics.title: 1. Physical Quantities, Units and Measurement
outcomes: Recall base quantities and SI units
Use SI prefixes from nano to tera
Know orders of magnitude from atom to Earth
Choose measuring instruments by range and precision
Distinguish scalars and vectors and add vectors graphically

topics.title: 2. Kinematics
outcomes: Define speed and velocity and calculate average speed
Calculate acceleration from change in velocity over time
Plot and interpret displacement-time and velocity-time graphs
Find displacement from the area under a velocity-time graph
Know free-fall acceleration is constant at about 10 m/s²

topics.title: 3. Dynamics
outcomes: Distinguish mass and weight using W = mg
Apply Newton's laws, including action-reaction pairs and F = ma
Draw free body diagrams and solve three-force equilibrium graphically
Explain friction, inertia and resistive forces
Describe falling with or without air resistance, including terminal velocity

topics.title: 4. Turning Effects of Forces
outcomes: Apply the principle of moments to bodies in equilibrium
Treat weight as acting at the centre of gravity
Relate centre of gravity position to stability

topics.title: 5. Pressure
outcomes: Explain pressure transmission in hydraulic systems
Explain how a liquid column measures atmospheric pressure

topics.title: 6. Energy
outcomes: Calculate kinetic and gravitational potential energy
Calculate work done, power and efficiency

topics.title: 7. Kinetic Particle Model of Matter
outcomes: Explain states of matter using particle arrangement and motion
Use Brownian motion as evidence of random particle movement
Link temperature to average kinetic energy
Explain gas pressure using particle motion

topics.title: 8. Thermal Processes
outcomes: Explain heat flow until thermal equilibrium
Explain factors affecting the rate of radiation
Apply thermal processes to everyday examples

topics.title: 9. Thermal Properties of Matter
outcomes: Use Q = mcΔθ and define specific heat capacity
Explain melting and boiling without temperature change
Use Q = mL for latent heat

topics.title: 10. General Properties of Waves
outcomes: Describe wave motion and energy transfer
Explain sound as compressions and rarefactions needing a medium
Relate loudness to amplitude and pitch to frequency; echoes and ultrasound

topics.title: 11. Electromagnetic Spectrum
outcomes: All EM waves are transverse and travel at the same speed in vacuum
Order the spectrum by wavelength and frequency

topics.title: 12. Light
outcomes: Use sin i / sin r and refractive index
Explain critical angle and total internal reflection, including optical fibres
Draw ray diagrams for a thin converging lens

topics.title: 13. Static Electricity
outcomes: Like charges repel, unlike charges attract
Explain charging by rubbing and by induction
Describe hazards and uses such as the electrostatic precipitator

topics.title: 14. Current of Electricity
outcomes: Use R = V/I and how length and area affect resistance
Sketch and interpret I-V graphs for ohmic conductors, filament lamps and diodes

topics.title: 15. D.C. Circuits
outcomes: Apply current and p.d. rules for series and parallel circuits
Use potential dividers with thermistors and LDRs

topics.title: 16. Practical Electricity
outcomes: Use P = VI and E = VIt and calculate cost in kWh
Explain fuses, circuit breakers, earthing and double insulation
Describe live, neutral and earth wiring in a plug

topics.title: 17. Magnetism
outcomes: Draw field patterns of bar magnets

topics.title: 18. Electromagnetism
outcomes: Draw fields around wires and solenoids
Use Fleming's left-hand rule for force on a current
Explain how a d.c. motor works, including the split-ring commutator

topics.title: 19. Electromagnetic Induction
outcomes: A changing magnetic field induces an e.m.f. that opposes the change
Describe an a.c. generator and its output graph
Explain why power is transmitted at high voltage

topics.title: 20. Radioactivity
outcomes: Use nuclide notation and write decay equations
Compare alpha, beta and gamma radiation
Discuss uses and hazards of radioactivity

syllabus.notes: Paper 3 is a practical test with no reference materials; an approved calculator may be used in all papers.

syllabus.subject: Singapore–Cambridge Secondary Education Certificate (2027) G3 Chemistry

assessment.format: 40 compulsory multiple-choice items, with a copy of the Periodic Table printed in the paper.
Section A: compulsory structured questions (70 marks), including a data-based question worth 8–12 marks. Section B: choose one of two questions (10 marks).
A variable number of compulsory practical questions, some possibly testing planning and data analysis without apparatus.

topics.title: 1. Experimental Chemistry
outcomes: Name apparatus for measuring time, temperature, mass and volume
Suggest suitable apparatus for simple experiments, including gas drying, collection and rate measurements
Describe separation and purification methods for mixtures
Suggest separation methods for solid-solid, solid-liquid and liquid-liquid mixtures
Interpret paper chromatograms using known samples and Rf values
Use melting and boiling point data to identify substances and judge purity

topics.title: 2. The Particulate Nature of Matter
outcomes: Describe solids, liquids and gases using kinetic particle theory
Explain evidence for particle movement and everyday diffusion
Explain how molecular mass and temperature affect diffusion rate
State relative charges and approximate masses of subatomic particles
Describe atomic structure with nucleons and electron shells
Use nuclide notation, define isotopes, and deduce particle numbers

topics.title: 3. Chemical Bonding and Structure
outcomes: Describe ion formation and ionic bonding with dot-and-cross diagrams
Relate ionic lattice structure to properties of ionic compounds
Describe covalent bonding and deduce electron arrangements in molecules
Relate covalent structures (simple, macromolecular, giant) to properties
Describe metallic bonding and general properties of metals
Explain differences between elements, compounds, mixtures and alloys

topics.title: 4. Chemical Calculations
outcomes: Deduce formulae of simple and ionic compounds
Construct balanced equations with state symbols, including ionic equations
Define and calculate Ar, Mr and percentage mass of an element
Calculate empirical and molecular formulae, reacting masses and gas volumes
Apply solution concentration to volumetric (titration) results
Calculate percentage yield and percentage purity

topics.title: 5. Acid-Base Chemistry
outcomes: Describe acids and alkalis by the ions they produce and their indicator colours
Compare strong and weak acids, neutrality, and the pH scale
Describe acid reactions, neutralisation, and treating acidic soil with calcium hydroxide
Classify oxides as acidic, basic, amphoteric or neutral
Describe preparation, separation and purification of salts, and solubility rules
Describe the Haber Process, reversible reactions, and interpret industrial conditions

topics.title: 6. Qualitative Analysis
outcomes: Identify aqueous cations using sodium hydroxide and aqueous ammonia
Identify anions (carbonate, chloride, iodide, nitrate, sulfate) using specified tests
Identify gases (ammonia, carbon dioxide, chlorine, hydrogen, oxygen) using specified tests

topics.title: 7. Redox Chemistry
outcomes: Define redox by oxygen/hydrogen transfer, electron transfer and oxidation state
Identify redox reactions and test for oxidising and reducing agents
Describe electrolysis of molten and aqueous ionic compounds
Predict electrolysis products using selective discharge and construct electrode equations
Describe electroplating, copper purification, simple cells and hydrogen fuel cells

topics.title: 8. Patterns in the Periodic Table
outcomes: Describe the arrangement of elements by proton number and link position to electronic configuration
Describe periodic trends in metallic and non-metallic character
Describe trends in Groups 1, 17 and 18 and predict properties
Describe properties of transition elements, including their use as catalysts
Place metals in a reactivity series using reactions and experimental data
Describe rusting, its prevention, and sacrificial protection

topics.title: 9. Chemical Energetics
outcomes: Describe exothermic and endothermic reactions using enthalpy change
Represent energy changes with energy profile diagrams
Describe bond breaking as endothermic and bond making as exothermic
Explain overall enthalpy change using bond energy changes

topics.title: 10. Rate of Reactions
outcomes: Explain how concentration, pressure, particle size and temperature affect rate using collisions
Define catalysts and explain how they lower activation energy
Suggest a method to investigate a variable's effect on rate
Interpret experimental data on rate of reaction

topics.title: 11. Organic Chemistry
outcomes: Describe crude oil as a hydrocarbon mixture separated by fractional distillation
Describe alkanes and alkenes, their structures, naming, and reactions
Describe cracking and the manufacture of margarine
Describe alcohols, carboxylic acids and esters, including their reactions and naming
Describe polymers, addition and condensation polymerisation, and their uses
Describe plastic pollution, recycling methods, and related social and economic issues

topics.title: 12. Maintaining Air Quality
outcomes: State the composition of dry air
Name common air pollutants and their sources
Describe reactions used to reduce pollutants, including catalytic converters and calcium carbonate
Discuss effects of pollutants on health and environment, including acid rain and ozone depletion
Describe the carbon cycle and greenhouse gases with their effects

syllabus.notes: The Periodic Table is printed in Papers 1 and 2, Notes for Qualitative Analysis are printed in Paper 3, no notebooks or textbooks are allowed in Paper 3, and an approved calculator may be used in all papers.

syllabus.subject: G3 Biology

assessment.format: 40 compulsory multiple-choice items.
Section A (70 marks): compulsory structured, free-response and data-based questions; Section B (10 marks): answer one of two free-response questions.
Two to three compulsory practical questions, which may include planning and data analysis.

topics.title: Cell Structure and Organisation
outcomes: Identify cell structures and organelles and their functions
Explain how specialised cells suit their functions

topics.title: Movement of Substances
outcomes: Describe diffusion in nutrient uptake and gas exchange
Describe osmosis and its effects on plant and animal tissues
Explain active transport against a concentration gradient

topics.title: Biological Molecules
outcomes: State the roles of carbohydrates, fats and proteins
Carry out food tests for starch, reducing sugars, protein and fats
Explain how enzymes work: active site, activation energy, specificity
Explain effects of temperature and pH on enzymes

topics.title: Nutrition in Humans
outcomes: Describe the digestive system and peristalsis
Describe the functions of digestive enzymes
State the roles of the liver and hepatic portal vein

topics.title: Transport in Humans
outcomes: Relate arteries, veins and capillaries to their functions
State the components of blood and their roles
Use ABO blood groups for transfusions
Describe the heart and the cardiac cycle

topics.title: Respiration in Humans
outcomes: Describe breathing and gas exchange in alveoli
State the effects of tobacco smoke
Give equations for aerobic and anaerobic respiration

topics.title: Excretion in Humans
outcomes: Outline ultrafiltration and selective reabsorption in the nephron

topics.title: Homeostasis, Co-ordination and Response in Humans
outcomes: Explain blood glucose control by insulin and glucagon
Describe type 2 diabetes and its management
Outline ADH and the reflex arc
Describe the eye and the pupil reflex

topics.title: Infectious Diseases in Humans
outcomes: Describe viruses and bacteria and how they spread
Explain why antibiotics don't work on viruses and how resistance develops

topics.title: Nutrition and Transport in Flowering Plants
outcomes: State the photosynthesis equation and limiting factors
Explain transpiration and factors affecting it

topics.title: Organisms and their Environment
outcomes: Describe energy flow, food chains and pyramids
Explain global warming and how to reduce it

topics.title: Molecular Genetics
outcomes: Describe DNA structure and base pairing
Explain genetic engineering, e.g. insulin from bacteria
Discuss benefits and ethics of genetic engineering

topics.title: Reproduction
outcomes: Describe pollination and fertilisation in flowers
Describe human reproduction and the menstrual cycle

topics.title: Inheritance
outcomes: Explain gene, allele and key genetic terms
Use genetic diagrams for monohybrid crosses

syllabus.notes: Paper 3 is a practical test without notebooks or textbooks; an approved calculator may be used in all papers.
